The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the Base Rate at its current level (5.00%) for the intermeeting period.
The Bank of Korea
Monetary Policy Decision
The domestic economy exhibits signs of a slowdown in its pace of expansion.
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the Base Rate at its current level (5.00%) for the intermeeting period.
While exports continue to post robust growth, domestic demand has slackened.

There still remains a high degree of uncertainty surrounding future economic developments, largely due to the run-up in international oil prices, the international financial market unrest and the US economic slowdown.
(The following is an English translation of the Monetary Policy Committee statement.)
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the Base Rate at its current level (5.00%) for the intermeeting period.
Consumer price inflation has picked up its pace, mainly influenced by high oil prices.
The upward trend of real estate prices has slowed down somewhat.
The domestic economy exhibits signs of a slowdown in its pace of expansion.
While exports continue to post robust growth, domestic demand has slackened.
Liquidity is still ample in the financial markets and financial institutions' lending continues to show a steady increase.

There still remains a high degree of uncertainty surrounding future economic developments, largely due to the run-up in international oil prices, the international financial market unrest and the US economic slowdown.
Meanwhile, long-term market interest rates have shown a sharp rise.
